microtheory.name: genetics_molecular
microtheory.definition: Genetic information storage, transmission, expression. DNA, RNA, proteins, central dogma, gene regulation, mutation types, epigenetics. The molecular substrate of heredity. Substrate analogue: substrate's persistent graph state as 'genetic' substrate; expression dynamics as transcription/translation analogue.

concepts.name: central_dogma
concepts.definition: Crick 1958. Information flows DNA → RNA → protein. Generally not backwards (though reverse transcriptase exists). Substrate analogue: substrate's seed → runtime → output flow.

concepts.name: transcription
concepts.definition: DNA → RNA. RNA polymerase reads template strand. Substrate analogue: substrate's reading seed Mts into active state.

concepts.name: translation_genetics
concepts.definition: mRNA → protein at ribosome. Codon table maps triplets to amino acids. Substrate analogue: substrate's Term-tree → action.

concepts.name: codon
concepts.definition: Three nucleotides specifying one amino acid (or stop). 64 codons, 20 amino acids. Substrate analogue: substrate's lexical-to-Concept mapping primitive.

concepts.name: genetic_code
concepts.definition: Mapping codons → amino acids. Nearly universal across life. Substrate analogue: substrate's universal symbol-to-meaning mapping.

concepts.name: ribosome
concepts.definition: Molecular machine performing translation. RNA + protein complex. Substrate analogue: substrate's Term-evaluator.

concepts.name: nucleotide
concepts.definition: DNA/RNA monomer. Phosphate + sugar + base (A,T,C,G in DNA; A,U,C,G in RNA). Substrate analogue: substrate's primitive symbol.

concepts.name: base_pairing
concepts.definition: A-T (or A-U) + C-G complementarity. Foundation of replication + transcription. Substrate analogue: substrate's complementarity in matching.

concepts.name: double_helix
concepts.definition: DNA structure. Two antiparallel strands. Watson + Crick + Franklin 1953. Substrate analogue: substrate's paired structural representation.

concepts.name: chromosome
concepts.definition: Packaged DNA. Humans have 46 (23 pairs). Substrate analogue: substrate's organizational Mt cluster.

concepts.name: chromatin
concepts.definition: DNA + protein packaging. Euchromatin (active) vs heterochromatin (silent). Substrate analogue: substrate's accessible vs locked Mts.

concepts.name: gene_expression
concepts.definition: Process by which gene produces functional product (typically protein). Regulated. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt activation.

concepts.name: transcription_factor
concepts.definition: Protein binding DNA + regulating transcription. Activates or represses. Substrate analogue: substrate's policy_filter agent.

concepts.name: promoter
concepts.definition: DNA region where transcription begins. RNA polymerase binds. Substrate analogue: substrate's reflex trigger pattern.

concepts.name: enhancer
concepts.definition: DNA region binding transcription factors + boosting transcription. Distal to gene. Substrate analogue: substrate's modulating context.

concepts.name: operon
concepts.definition: Bacterial gene-cluster regulated together. Jacob + Monod's lac operon. Substrate analogue: substrate's co-regulated Mt cluster.

concepts.name: feedback_loop_gene
concepts.definition: Gene product affecting its own expression. Negative (limit) or positive (commit). Substrate analogue: substrate's correction self-modification.

concepts.name: mutation_types
concepts.definition: Point (single base), insertion, deletion, duplication, inversion, translocation. Different consequences. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt modification types.

concepts.name: point_mutation
concepts.definition: Single base change. Synonymous (silent), missense (different amino acid), nonsense (premature stop). Substrate analogue: substrate's single-attribute change.

concepts.name: frameshift_mutation
concepts.definition: Insertion/deletion not divisible by 3 shifts reading frame. Usually devastating. Substrate analogue: substrate's structural disruption.

concepts.name: loss_of_function
concepts.definition: Mutation eliminating gene function. Often recessive. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt deactivation.

concepts.name: gain_of_function
concepts.definition: Mutation conferring new function. Often dominant. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt extension.

concepts.name: mendelian_genetics
concepts.definition: Mendel 1866. Inheritance via discrete factors. Dominance, segregation, independent assortment. Substrate analogue: substrate's discrete trait inheritance.

concepts.name: dominant_recessive
concepts.definition: Dominant: expressed in heterozygote. Recessive: only homozygote. Substrate analogue: substrate's expression-priority.

concepts.name: allele
concepts.definition: Alternative form of a gene at given locus. Substrate analogue: substrate's variant of Concept.

concepts.name: polygenic_trait
concepts.definition: Trait determined by many genes. Continuous variation. Substrate analogue: substrate's multi-Concept emergent property.

concepts.name: epigenetic_modification
concepts.definition: Heritable changes not in DNA sequence. DNA methylation, histone modification, non-coding RNAs. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-level state above graph.

concepts.name: dna_methylation
concepts.definition: Addition of methyl group to cytosine. Silences genes. Inherited through cell divisions. Substrate analogue: substrate's policy_filter persistence.

concepts.name: histone_modification
concepts.definition: Chemical changes to histone proteins. Acetylation activates; methylation can do either. Substrate analogue: substrate's accessibility modification.

concepts.name: horizontal_gene_transfer
concepts.definition: Transfer between unrelated organisms. Common in bacteria. Antibiotic resistance spread. Substrate analogue: substrate-substrate Mt borrowing.

concepts.name: crispr_cas9
concepts.definition: Bacterial adaptive immunity adapted as gene editing tool. Doudna + Charpentier. Substrate analogue: substrate's targeted Mt modification.

concepts.name: gene_regulatory_network
concepts.definition: Genes regulating each other. Boolean network models. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-Mt regulation graph.

concepts.name: robustness_canalization
concepts.definition: Waddington. Developmental + genetic systems buffered against perturbation. Substrate analogue: substrate's drift-resistance.

rules.name: central_dogma_constrains_info_flow
rules.head: the substrate processes genetic information
rules.body: the standard direction is genotype → expression → phenotype. Reverse flow rare. Substrate's seed → runtime → output.

rules.name: regulation_determines_when_genes_express
rules.head: the substrate has the same genetic content
rules.body: transcription factors + epigenetic state determine which genes express when. Substrate's contextual Mt activation.

rules.name: mutation_provides_variation_for_selection
rules.head: the substrate undergoes natural selection
rules.body: mutation provides the heritable variation. Without variation, no selection. Substrate's stochastic Mt modification source.

rules.name: epigenetic_changes_can_be_inherited
rules.head: the substrate has acquired Mt-level changes during life
rules.body: some can transmit to descendants without DNA change. Substrate's accumulated state surviving structural transfer.

rules.name: horizontal_transfer_spreads_traits_outside_inheritance
rules.head: two substrates encounter each other
rules.body: Mts can transfer between them outside normal inheritance. Substrate's cross-substrate borrowing.
